question: What is the ruling on: a fleet of one reshapes the pickup phase?
why_it_blocks: answered before the question door existed; migrated into the corpus so the system reads its Q&A in one place
answer:
Code Mother isn't a builder. Aider turned out not to be a good enough builder. so we have one builder, you. so if something is waiting, it's not _nobody has taken it up_ as much as it is _cc has not had time yet_. a fleet of one so far. :)
So that being said: :waiting for 'waiting for somebody to do me' (as in TICKETME BUILDME etc) is fine. :inprocess as a state for 'i'm doing it now' is groovy. :queued <-- this is new, and means it's blocked by another ticket's completion. :hold <-- this is new, and this is the state for our 'cognition' tickets. they're on hold until the other work is done. :blocked <-- this is new, and means there's a problem and it can't move forward and you can't sort on your own what to do with it next.
nothing passes a gate with prose. an inspector will not allow it. not only has to have a field, but valid data to the limits of detection of deterministic code. we can add more sieves as needed.
Of course hold is a graveyard risk, but it's in the reports. it shows up. and it should show up in the operator inbox specifically so the operator is kept aware "you've got a hold on these".
in process should be AUTOMATICALLY cleared in post build part of the sail skill.
stateless read on in-process makes sense to me
exactly so. the source of truth is the picture in my head. everything else is working toward a more and more faithful implementation of that.
